recommendedTextbook.title: Essential Government for Senior Secondary Schools
recommendedTextbook.author: C. C. Dibie
recommendedTextbook.approvedBy: NERDC & Lagos State Ministry of Basic Education

subtopics: The Hausa-Fulani centralized emirate system: Emir, Waziri, Galadima, Madawaki
The Yoruba Oyo constitutional monarchy: Alaafin, Oyomesi, Bashorun, Ogboni society
The Igbo acephalous segmented democracy: Ofo titleholders, Umuada, age grades, village assembly
objectives: Compare administrative centralization in the Sokoto Caliphate with Yoruba checks and balances
Explain the decentralized republican decision-making process among the pre-colonial Igbo
Analyze how pre-colonial political traditions continue to shape modern Nigerian politics

topics.topic: British Colonial Administration and the Indirect Rule System
subtopics: Meaning, reasons, and structure of Indirect Rule under Lord Lugard
Application and success in Northern Nigeria
Implementation difficulties and resistance in Western and Eastern Nigeria (Aba Women's Riots of 1929)
objectives: Enumerate 5 reasons why Lord Lugard introduced Indirect Rule in Nigeria
Explain why Indirect Rule failed in Eastern Nigeria (warrant chiefs controversy)
Assess negative political and economic legacies of British colonial rule in Nigeria

subtopics: The 1914 Amalgamation and the Nigerian Council of Lord Lugard
The Clifford Constitution of 1922: Introduction of elective principle and first political party (NNDP)
Richards Constitution (1946), Macpherson Constitution (1951), and Lyttelton Constitution (1954) federal structure
objectives: Highlight the revolutionary significance of the 1922 elective principle
Explain how the Richards Constitution divided Nigeria into 3 administrative regions
Identify the 1954 Lyttelton Constitution as the formal foundation of Nigerian federalism

subtopics: Meaning and factors that stimulated Nigerian nationalism (post-WWII returnees, West African Pilot, Atlantic Charter)
Early nationalist movements: NYM, NCNC, AG, NPC
Contributions of Herbert Macaulay, Nnamdi Azikiwe, Obafemi Awolowo, and Ahmadu Bello
objectives: Analyze external and internal catalysts of anti-colonial nationalist agitation
Examine the role of the nationalist press in mobilizing public opinion against colonialism
Assess the London Constitutional Conferences leading to Nigerian Independence on October 1, 1960
